internship.heading: Professional Internship
internship.subheading: SOC incident triage automation: designing and shipping a production Python microservice pipeline for Managed Detection & Response.
internship.title: Automating SOC Incident Triage — VanRoey (Dynamate)
internship.context: VanRoey (Dynamate) is a leading Managed Service Provider. Their SOC team was handling security alerts manually — analysts pivoted between SentinelOne, VirusTotal and internal databases for each incident.
internship.objectives: The primary goal was to eliminate the triage bottleneck by automating Threat Intelligence enrichment and ticketing workflows end-to-end.
internship.businessCase: Automated triage reduces Mean Time to Respond (MTTR), eliminates licensing costs for third-party SOAR platforms, and allows SOC analysts to focus on deep investigation rather than data pivot.
internship.methodology: I followed an agile approach, evaluating MISP vs OpenCTI, discovering vendor API bugs through R&D collaboration, and implementing an event-driven architecture with high-fidelity UAT.
internship.synopsis:
During my internship at VanRoey (Dynamate), I was tasked with addressing the slow Mean Time to Respond (MTTR) caused by manual incident triage. Analysts were pivoting between disconnected tools for every alert. 

I architected a resilient, asynchronous event-driven pipeline using FastAPI, RabbitMQ, Redis, and Docker. I integrated independent Threat Intelligence feeds (MISP, CIRCL) rechtstreeks in de workflows. By deploying custom Python microservices, I automated IoC extraction and enrichment, generating actionable tickets in Datto Autotask with sub-30-second turnaround. This solution not only optimized operations but also eliminated recurring SOAR platform licensing costs.
internship.projectPlanDesc: Objectives, business case, planning, and progress reporting.
internship.thesisDesc: Full realization thesis — 5W1H approach, architecture, and outcomes.
internship.reflectionDesc: Personal learning outcomes, growth, and critical reflection.

timeline.step1Desc: Deployed both via Docker; chose MISP for bulk-API performance
timeline.step2Desc: Confirmed STIX 2.1 parser defect with S1 R&D — no patch timeline
timeline.step3Desc: 85% payload reduction vs REST; solved HTTPS with HAProxy + Let's Encrypt
timeline.step4Desc: Black-box debugging & Jinja complexity ruled out low-code
timeline.step5Desc: FastAPI · RabbitMQ · Redis · Docker — deployed to production
